sections.title: Language Exchange Registration
sections.context: A student is inquiring about a weekly language exchange event at the University's Student Services office.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Good morning! Welcome to the Student Services desk. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Hi there. I saw a poster about the 'Polyglot Hub' language exchange event. I'm really keen on improving my speaking skills, so I'd like to sign up for that.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: That's great! It's one of our most popular programs. I just need to take down some details first. Can I have your full name, please?

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Sure, it's Liam Hennessey.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Could you spell your surname for me, Liam?

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Yes, it's H-E-double N-E-double S-E-Y.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Thank you. And do you have your student ID number handy?

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Yes, it's right here... let me see... it is LH9982.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Got it. Now, which language is your native one? We need to know so we can pair you with the right partners.

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: My mother is from Madrid, so Spanish is my first language, though I've lived in Australia for a few years now.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Perfect. And which language are you looking to practice? I assume it's English?

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Actually, I'm quite comfortable with English. I'm currently studying French for my degree. I’d say I’m at an Intermediate level... oh, wait, I actually just received my results for the proficiency test last week and I've moved up to the Upper-Intermediate level. So please put that down instead.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Well done! That's impressive. Now, we have two sessions running. One is on Tuesday afternoons and the other is on Thursday evenings. Which one would you prefer?

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Tuesday would usually be better... but I've just realized I have a football match every Tuesday for the rest of the term. So, I'll have to go with Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Thursday it is. Now, let me give you some information about the venue. It used to be held in the Student Union building, but because of the renovations, we've moved it to the Central Library. It's on the second floor in the quiet study zone, which we've reserved for the event.

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Okay, the Central Library. And what time does it start? I finish my last lecture at 6:00 PM.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: The doors open at 6:00, but the structured conversation sessions don't actually begin until 6:30 PM. That gives everyone half an hour to grab a drink and settle in.

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: That's perfect. Do I need to bring anything specific? A dictionary, perhaps?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: A dictionary isn't necessary because we provide vocabulary sheets. However, we do recommend that students bring a notebook to jot down new phrases or idioms they learn during the evening.

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: Right, I'll make sure to bring one. Are there any rules I should be aware of?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Just one major one to ensure everyone focuses on speaking: we ask all participants to put away their smartphones during the 45-minute speaking block. It really helps with the immersion.

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: That makes sense. It's too easy to just look up a word on a phone instead of trying to explain it. Is there any cost?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: It's free for all students! In fact, we actually have a loyalty scheme. If you attend five sessions in a row, we give out vouchers that you can use for free coffee at the campus cafe.

transcript.speaker: Liam
transcript.text: That's a great incentive! Thanks for the help, Sarah.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Liam. See you on Thursday!
